title: Decentralized canary hedging router for spotty-regions and tenant quarantining
creator: Maya Thompson
summary: Implement a decentralized routing layer that hedges canary traffic across unreliable regions and isolates affected tenant islands for fast evacuation. The router should support A/B experiments, shadow traffic mirroring, and automated rollback triggers while preserving KV cache locality where possible and respecting tiered capacity buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Router can route a canary cohort across two regions simultaneously with hedged fan-out and collect per-variant metrics within a single request path
When region RTT/p95 or error_rate exceeds configured thresholds, router fails over to next tier without dropping requests more than 2% in steady state
Tenant quarantining mode can redirect all traffic from a impacted tenant to a cold-safe model variant in <30s and create a pinned eviction plan

Shadow traffic pipeline mirrors 100% of selected traffic to the new variant with no more than 5% added tail latency to production path (measured in synthetic tests), and shadowed KV cache warm-ups are recorded

Auto-rollback triggers are functional: latency p95 regressions >50%, absolute error-rate delta >0.5%, or embedding-score drift >3% on evaluation prompts lead to automated controlled rollback and an incident ticket creation
End-to-end integration tests demonstrate compatibility scoring rejects variant if incompatible with runtime proto or required ops and surfaces clear reason codes
design_notes: Use probabilistic hedging: route X% traffic to canary region and (1-X)% to primary; if canary shows improvement, increase weight on 10% schedule
Decentralized decisioning: each edge-routing node runs a small policy engine (Rust) with configuration from central control plane; avoids single-controller latency during network partitions
Compatibility scoring: binary + weighted feature flags (e.g., kv-cache-preserve, quantization-profile, kv-shard-layout). Score thresholds are tunable per-customer

Tiered capacity model: map variants into capacity buckets (hot, warm, cold). Router prefers hot variants when tenant priority is high; fallback paths can accept warm/cold with user-configured latency budget
KV cache preservation: on spillover, attempt soft-warm: forward request to target variant while routing a background warm-up copy to preserve cold-start latency window
Telemetry: instrument per-variant p50/p95/p99, error types, semantic-quality checks (via small eval set), and cache-hit ratio. Use sampling for full payload capture
Trade-offs: decentralized checks reduce central availability dependencies but increase config distribution complexity. Chosen for better fail-safety in regional flare-ups
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with infra and product. Agreed on priority signals (p95 latency, 5xx rate, eval-score drift). Action: Proto policy spec (Confluence) [https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEP/canary-hedging-proto].

2026-02-28: Initial policy engine PoC (rust) implemented. Local simulation harness shows hedging reduces bad-canary exposure by 60% in synthetic outage tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/412

2026-03-03: Design review with SRE and Security. Decided against central live traffic shadow for privacy-sensitive tenants; added tenant-label gating. Security review requested for control-plane config endpoints.

2026-03-06: Telemetry schema added to metrics repo. Dashboards proto created in Grafana: runtime/canary-hedging-overview and runtime/tenant-evacuation. Dashboards link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CanaryHedging/overview
2026-03-10: Integration tests for region failover and capacity-bucket spillback passing in staging (see CI run #885). Next: broaden shadow traffic runs to 2% of traffic and validate KV warm-up traces
decisions: Adopt decentralized edge policy engine (Rust) instead of centralized policy gRPC calls to reduce control-plane-induced amplification during net partitions
Expose tenant quarantining as an operator-triggered and automated mode; automated mode uses conservative thresholds and requires post-mortem alerting
Require compatibility scoring for all variants; incompatible variants will be fenced and not receive production traffic until human-approved
Auto-rollback will not delete variant resources; it will shift traffic and create a rollback artifact with metrics and logs for post-incident analysis
runbook: Detect: automated alerts fire when canary p95 > baseline*1.5 OR error-rate delta > 0.5%
Mitigate: switch tenant to quarantine plan via 'router quarantine <tenant-id>' which pins variant to cold-safe fallback within 30s
Rollback: trigger automated shift to previous stable variant weight with staged 10% reroutes over 2 minutes
Incident: system creates incident ticket and uploads captured traces and eval diffs to ticket automatically
test_plan: Unit tests for policy engine decision paths (moskito), compatibility scoring, and eviction-planner
Staging experiments: run 2% shadow traffic mirrored for 48 hours; collect semantic eval on sampled outputs
Chaos tests: simulate regional network partitions and GPU OOM; ensure router evacuates tenants and respects capacity buckets
Load test: validate hedged routing under 2x baseline traffic with <2% request drop and <20% added p95 latency
notes: Follow-up: product wants an A/B UI for non-technical SREs to configure hedging weights per-customer
Consider adding a cost-signal into routing policy to prefer lower-cost variants when quality delta < 0.5%
Ask infra: persistent config distribution needs a rollout window to avoid large fan-outs; propose staggered 1-minute TTL pushes
